The experimental log human plasma protein binding (% unbound) value for the following molecule NC1CCC(C(=O)N2CCC(c3c[nH]c4ncccc34)CC2)C1 is 1.9173952. What is the experimental log human plasma protein binding (% unbound) value of a closely related molecule NC1CCCC(C(=O)N2CCC(c3c[nH]c4ncccc34)CC2)C1.
The protocol of the experimental assay is as follows: Human plasmas in potassium EDTA (BIOIVT Westbury, NY) were used in the RED (rapid equilibrium dialysis) device plates (ThermoFisher Scientific Waltham, MA) to determine the plasma protein binding values; the compounds were tested at a concentration of 1~$\mu$ M and spiked in rat or human plasmas (at least 10 donors); 300~$\mu$ L of spiked plasma samples were added to the donor chambers in the RED device (RED tubes), and 500~$\mu$ L aliquots of 100 mM potassium phosphate and 150 mM NaCl at pH 7.4 (phosphate buffer) were added to the corresponding receiving side of the RED device inserts; after 4 h of incubation at 37~$^{\circ}$C with 5\% carbon dioxide, 50~$\mu$ L of each sample from donor and receiver sides was removed for analysis and placed in a 96-well plate containing 200~$\mu$ L of protein precipitation solution (50/50 acetonitrile/methanol with an internal standard); all plasma and buffer samples were matrix matched, vortex mixed for 30 s, and centrifuged at 3900 rpm for 10 min; 50~$\mu$ L aliquots of supernatant were transferred into individual wells in a 96-well plate containing 200~$\mu$ L of 0.1\% formic acid in 90/10 water/acetonitrile and vortex mixed gently; samples were analyzed utilizing LC-MS/MS coupled with a high throughput injection system; plasma protein binding (PPB) percent unbound from the RED device was calculated as
\begin{align*}
\% \text{Unbound} &= \frac{\text{avgPAR in the buffer side}}{\text{avgPAR in the plasma side}} \times 100,
\end{align*}
where avgPAR is the average peak area ratio of the analyte to internal standard.

At the conclusion of your response, provide the final answer in the format: ## Answer: floating_point_number ## The final result should be a single floating point number.
